text: The objection that "existence is not a real predicate" was first raised by Anselm himself as a caution against his own ontological argument.
explanation: False. "Existence is not a predicate" is Kant's objection to the ontological argument in the Critique of Pure Reason, not Anselm's. Anselm treats existence in reality as a great-making feature; it is Kant who denies that existence adds anything to a concept of a thing.
